---
title: "Fuzzy Numbers: A Value with a Profile"
---

“About twenty-seven” places a number within a neighborhood of acceptable descriptions.

The center matters, but so does how quickly the description stops fitting as we move away. A fuzzy number can preserve that shape.

## 🔰 Build one number with a profile {#sec-sample-fuzzy-numbers-build-one-number-with-a-profile}

For a simple triangular example, define

$$
\mu_{\widetilde x}(v)
=
\max\!\left(0,\ 1-\frac{|v-27|}{5}\right).
$$

Its membership is one at 27, decreases linearly on either side, and reaches zero at 22 and 32.

Some evaluations make the definition tangible:

- $\mu_{\widetilde x}(27)=1$.
- $\mu_{\widetilde x}(26)=0.8$.
- $\mu_{\widetilde x}(29.5)=0.5$.
- $\mu_{\widetilde x}(33)=0$.

The input $v$ is a candidate numerical value. The output is how well it fits this extended numerical description.

In the simple family used here, a fuzzy number attains full membership and every positive membership threshold selects a bounded closed interval. Arbitrary fuzzy sets, such as a description with two separated peaks, need not satisfy this interval-shaped contract.

## 🏵 Marks and auras make the description readable {#sec-sample-fuzzy-numbers-marks-and-auras-make-the-description-readable}

The presentation's notation

$$
\widetilde x=P(M)\{A\}
$$

invites three declarations: profile, representative mark, and aura.

For our example we can state:

- **Profile:** triangular membership.
- **Mark:** the peak $M=27$.
- **Aura:** half-width $A=5$.

The aura here is a half-width, with the same units as the numerical values. It is not a standard deviation. Another profile or another aura definition would produce another object.

The notation carries a useful architecture once its components have names and contracts.

## ⚙️ Ask how strict the description should be {#sec-sample-fuzzy-numbers-ask-how-strict-the-description-should-be}

Choose a membership threshold $0<\alpha\leq1$ and keep values whose membership reaches it:

$$
[\widetilde x]_\alpha
=
\{v:\mu_{\widetilde x}(v)\geq\alpha\}.
$$

This is an **alpha-cut**: an ordinary set selected from a graded one.

For the triangle,

$$
[\widetilde x]_\alpha
=
[\,27-5(1-\alpha),\ 27+5(1-\alpha)\,].
$$

At $\alpha=0.5$, the accepted interval is $[24.5,29.5]$. At $\alpha=1$, only 27 remains.

The threshold is a membership requirement. It is not a confidence level or a probability of coverage.

## 💡 The same shorthand can hide different objects {#sec-sample-fuzzy-numbers-the-same-shorthand-can-hide-different-objects}

The notation $27\pm5$ could describe:

- Hard bounds from 22 to 32.
- A mean of 27 with standard deviation 5 under a specified probability law.
- A confidence interval produced by a sampling procedure.
- Our triangular membership profile.

The shorthand leaves those meanings unresolved. Choosing a familiar formula before choosing the meaning would settle the wrong question.

The broad *Fuzzy Number* of the slides can remain the inspiration for an extended-value architecture. Within calculations, attach the uncertainty type explicitly.

## ☯ Transform the whole description {#sec-sample-fuzzy-numbers-transform-the-whole-description}

If we shift every candidate value upward by three, the new fuzzy number has peak 30 and the same half-width five:

$$
\mu_{\widetilde y}(v)=\mu_{\widetilde x}(v-3).
$$

Each alpha-cut shifts by three as well. We have transported the complete membership profile, rather than choosing one representative value and discarding its neighborhood.

Producing one number from that profile requires another operation. [Fuzzy Generators](fuzzy-generators.qmd) gives that operation its own page.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Try the idea {#sec-sample-fuzzy-numbers-try-the-idea}

For the triangular description centered at 27 with half-width 5, find the $\alpha=0.8$ cut. What happens to it after shifting all values upward by three?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Work it through {#sec-sample-fuzzy-numbers-work-it-through}

The half-width of the cut is $5(1-0.8)=1$, so it is $[26,28]$. After the shift it is $[29,31]$. The grade threshold has stayed the same while the accepted numerical values moved.
:::
